title: Ionta competitive research: current products and UX patterns
scope: Freelancer-first relationship and client-work management. Channels: Gmail and WhatsApp; core product concepts: People, Inbox, Today, Tasks, Ask ledger, AI Advisor, and proposed Work Clusters.
method: Public primary documentation and visible product screenshots. Confirmed features are separated from UX hypotheses. A screenshot may depict a different version from the current feature docs.

competitors.name: folk CRM
competitors.focus: Contact-centric activity timeline; AI recap and smart fields
verified: Email and WhatsApp interactions are available on a contact profile.
Recap Assistant summarizes latest interactions, decisions and next steps on demand.
A mobile contacts app is documented from July 2026.
limitations: Recaps are generated on demand and require refresh.
Designed around sales/networking; freelancer delivery tracking not demonstrated.
WhatsApp integration scope is plan-dependent (Standard limits synced accounts).
ionta_questions: Is Ionta's client status persistent and operational rather than just recap text?
Can a follow-up be checked off and reopened on the same client?
How do linked emails/WhatsApp become a single client work unit?

competitors.name: Moxie V4
verified: Inbox Messages combines email, text and call history; Tickets manage client requests.
From a conversation, users can create a Project, Task, Ticket or Opportunity with source context.
Client/contact page combines related emails, texts, calls and tickets; linked tickets/tasks preserve context.
Moxie has AI summaries and MCP integrations for client/project work.
limitations: This is not proof of personal WhatsApp channel integration.
Work creation is a deliberate user action; automation across fragmented threads is not established by these docs.
ionta_questions: Could Ionta's Work Cluster merge successive changes automatically rather than duplicating records?
Can an Ask remain separate from the delivery Task while sharing status and provenance?
How does client-side waiting/approval state become visible in Today?

competitors.name: Missive
competitors.focus: Conversation to work; inbox and task statuses; AI extraction
verified: Unified inbox for email, SMS, WhatsApp and other channels.
Conversation tasks, subtasks and standalone tasks share one Tasks view.
AI Rules can add tasks from a message and label/summarize messages.
limitations: Being able to create tasks does not establish cross-thread project/work clustering.
ionta_questions: How can Ionta avoid Ask, Task and Work Cluster all looking like separate tasks?
Does a client-request remain visible as an event and as a live work item without duplication?

competitors.name: Front
competitors.focus: Contact conversations, waiting states, unified support inbox
verified: Contact Conversations can list email/text and other permitted channels by contact.
Inbox can be segmented into Open/Waiting/Resolved.
limitations: Contact tab groups by conversation rather than merging all message events into one timeline.
Designed primarily for team shared inbox workflows.
ionta_questions: Should waiting status be attached to a client, conversation or extracted work object?
How do users move between per-client history and priority queue?

competitors.name: Shortwave
competitors.focus: AI triage plan, proposed actions and follow-up queries
verified: AI assistant can suggest grouped inbox actions for approval.
Can identify action items from threads and follow-ups needing attention.
limitations: Email-centered rather than full Gmail/WhatsApp client workspace.
ionta_questions: Should AI recommendations first appear as reviewable suggested actions instead of automatically created tasks?
How does evidence/source appear with each suggestion?

competitors.name: Pylon
competitors.focus: Customer context, Waiting on You / Waiting on Customer operational status
verified: Cross-channel B2B support issues represent client work.
Issue boards present Waiting on You / Waiting on Customer groupings.
limitations: Enterprise support audience, not solo freelancer; ticket-centric.
ionta_questions: Use turn-state as a first-class status, not just unread.
Should waiting status be derived or editable?

competitors.name: Kustomer
verified: Customer timeline version 1 displays channel events chronologically on customer record.
limitations: The cited documentation is for timeline V1; do not claim this is the latest interface.
ionta_questions: How can Ionta merge source interactions into one chronology while distinguishing conversation vs work-event?
How is provenance shown on messages?

competitors.name: Sunsama
competitors.focus: Email becomes task, keeps original thread and syncs completion states
verified: Users can drag Gmail email into task list and embed email thread context.
Actions can be set on importing and completing linked tasks.
limitations: Explicit import; not designed around person-first omnichannel relationship or inferred Ask-ledger.
ionta_questions: How should Ionta capture source links and send action completion back to original message?
How do Today and Inbox stay synchronized without redundant reminders?

updated_competitive_risks: folk has mobile and AI Recap Assistant, contrary to earlier Ionta case study summary.
Moxie V4 now documents unified email/text/call Inbox, contact timeline and conversation-to-work conversion.
Missive now documents AI action-item extraction and three task types.
hypotheses_not_verified_as_unique: Persistent, multi-channel client turn-state with actionable follow-up, not merely interaction recap.
Automatic grouping of successive requests/revisions into one Work Cluster with delivery, reopen, cancellation history.
Unified Ask-ledger and Task representation without multiple duplicate entities.
next_research_tasks: Run an identical Sarah-client journey in folk, Missive and Moxie with source-linked screenshots.
Probe identity merge & WhatsApp ingestion boundaries, status inference, handling corrections and reopened requests.
Observe real freelancers to determine whether a client-centric view improves finding next action over inbox-first views.
